title: Capacity Safety-Net Workshop
summary: Workshop to define 'safety-net' for production: how much capacity headroom to hold, what automated fallbacks look like, and update runbooks for kernel/blocking OOM and cross-region failover. Decided to prototype a throttled-mode fallback and to run a targeted shake test next sprint.
action_items: Priya Malhotra: draft safety-net playbook and runbook edits - due 2026-03-20
Lucas Rivera: simulate KV cache warm-up and quantify latency penalty - due 2026-03-18
Ethan Park: prototype throttled-mode (reduced beam+quantization profile) for canary - due 2026-03-25
Sofia Gomez: add new dashboards for fallback incidence and token-cost delta - due 2026-03-22
Maya Thompson: align rollback policy with sales on enterprise SLAs and share updated doc - due 2026-03-17
next_steps: Schedule 2-hour shake test with Dedicated cluster next sprint
Circulate safety-net playbook draft to SRE and Support
Update runbooks and incident playbooks in docs repo
transcript:
Meeting: Capacity Safety-Net Workshop
Date/Time: 2026-03-06 09:30 PST
Duration: ~95 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Product), Lucas (SRE), Ethan (Runtime), Priya (Release), Sofia (Observability), Jonah (VP Eng), Rina (Infra), Amir (Security), Tessa (QA)

[00:00] Maya: All right, let's kick off. The goal today is to land on a pragmatic "safety-net" we can ship for Q2 — what to keep warm, how to degrade gracefully, and what the runbooks look like. I know this is a long one, so we'll try to capture decisions.

[00:24] Jonah: Quick context from leadership side — we've had two purple incidents in the last quarter that were tied to sudden spike + slow cache warm-up, and customers called out unpredictability. We need clear knobs for both cost and availability.

[00:48] Lucas: Yeah, from SRE perspective the OOM shock last month is the driver. We have modes today: full capacity, capped instances, and a hard failover to smaller models. But there's no middle ground — which causes big user-visible regression.

[01:15] Ethan: Right, and some of the smaller models don't preserve behavior — KV cash (sic), key-value cache warm-up is painful and latencies spike. Also, quantized kernel fallbacks are not always feature-parity; sometimes tokenization differences slip through.

[01:48] Priya: So proposed idea: a throttled-mode that reduces generation width (lower beams), applies conservative quant profile, and prioritizes prefix KV caching for recent sessions. That way latency doesn't tank and quality degrades gracefully.

[02:18] Amir: From security side we need to make sure telemetry in throttled-mode doesn't leak additional PII and that logs still meet our retention and KMS policies. If we're copying prefix caches or persisting these states during warm-up, encrypt everything.

[02:42] Sofia: Observability: we'll need a specific signal — 'fallback engaged' — and token-cost delta metric. Right now we have request-level latency and error; we don't tag fallbacks clearly.

[03:05] Rina: Ops question: where do these throttled instances run? On Dedicated pools or host them in a burst capacity? We need to decide because network topology matters for cache locality.

[03:30] Lucas: Prefer keeping them in Dedicated pools for the enterprise cohort until we have a validated behavior. Burst in Hosted for public customers could be a later rollout.

[04:01] Maya: Let's sketch SLO implications. If fallback is engaged, target 95th latency SLO is relaxed by 1.5x but availability SLO should stay. We should ensure post-fallback degrade cost is still within customer-specific commitments.

[04:33] Ethan: Implementation notes: runtime can route by per-route policy to a 'safety-net queue' that enforces lower max tokens and different kernel path. We'll need to add a profiler flag to simulate cache warm-up in dogfood.

[05:00] Tessa: QA asks for reproducible scenarios. We need test harnesses that emulate slow cache warm-up and concurrent KV misses. I can write a suite using the staging cluster.

[05:22] Jonah: Also consider a human-in-the-loop threshold: when fallback is frequent for a tenant, notify AE/CS and trigger a follow-up pilot for dedicated capacity.

[05:45] Priya: For rollback policy — do we auto-rollback the throttled-mode, or do we require manual intervention? I think auto-rollback after X minutes of stable metrics is fine, but dangerous if metrics are noisy.

[06:12] Lucas: Propose auto-rollback with hysteresis: engage fallback if latency above threshold for 2 minutes and CPU/GPU usage > 85% for 3 out of 5 samples; rollback when metrics calm for 10 minutes. We'll need to tune.

[06:45] Ethan: Caveat — for some models quantization can change decoding behavior; we should bind specific model-quant pairs as safe. We can maintain a catalog of certified model variants for safety-net use.

[07:10] Amir: Security review: any certified variants that change logits should be recorded in audit logs with KMS-wrapped keys for the model metadata. Compliance will want that for customers with strict audit needs.

[07:38] Sofia: Dashboards: I'll add a 'safety-net' tab that shows falls engaged, percent of requests, per-tenant impact, token-cost delta, and customer alerts. Also correlation with region and kernel fallback.

[08:05] Maya: Decision check — Are we aligned to prototype throttled-mode + safety-net dashboard + runbook updates as the deliverables?

[08:20] All: (affirmations)

[08:30] Maya: Great. Next: the playbook. Priya, can you own the first draft? Make it operational, include thresholds, notification steps, and escalation.

[08:45] Priya: Yes. I'll include exact metric names and runbook snippets.

[09:05] Lucas: I want to highlight stress-test approach. Rather than full chaos engineering, do a targeted "shake test" that artificially increases cold-starts by decommissioning 10% of key cache priming daemon and spiking traffic by 30% for 10 minutes.

[09:38] Ethan: We'll need a simulation mode in runtime to force KV miss rates up — I'll add a flag. Also add an experiment to compare warm-up time for different quant profiles so we can pick the fastest safe profile.

[10:02] Tessa: QA volunteer to run the shake test on a staging Dedicated pool next sprint. We'll schedule and capture histograms.

[10:24] Rina: Ops constraint: the staging Dedicated pool has different network egress; we must annotate tests to avoid billing surprises.

[10:40] Jonah: Also, product ask: include customer-visible messaging for when fallback occurs. Should be transparent but not scary — something like "Degraded mode engaged to preserve availability" with link to status.

[11:02] Priya: We'll template the message in CS playbook. AE can opt to suppress for specific customers if agreed.

[11:20] Amir: One more security point: telemetry in fallback mode should mask message content in logs if it's PII-sensitive. QA and SRE to coordinate on scrubbers.

[11:40] Lucas: Operational runbook sketch: detection -> engage throttled-mode -> notify on-call -> check KV miss rate and GPU temp -> if fallback persists > 30min escalate to infra + AE -> run prioritized remediation (cache warm-up, scale up, or targeted model switch).

[12:05] Ethan: On implementation timeline: prototype branch in 2 sprints, dogfood in internal prod in sprint 3, public beta in sprint 4 pending security sign-off.

[12:30] Maya: Risk list: 1) Quality regressions for edge prompts; 2) Mis-tuned auto-rollback causing flapping; 3) Unexpected token-cost changes for customers; 4) Audit gaps. We'll mitigate with certified variant list, hysteresis, cost monitoring, and audit hooks.

[12:58] Tessa: QA will add regression tests for the top-50 prompts we track in evals. That should catch user-visible quality deltas.

[13:18] Sofia: Observability will add a pre/post compare for embeddings/outputs on throttled samples when possible, to detect semantic drift. It will be sample-based for cost reasons.

[13:40] Priya: For the runbook doc location, propose /docs/runbooks/safety-net.md and link to incident page.

[13:56] Maya: Good. Last part — acceptance criteria for the prototype. We need three items: 1) fallback toggles executed with <10s config propagation, 2) measured P95 latency in throttled-mode within agreed SLO adjustment, 3) no data-leak from added telemetry.

[14:20] Jonah: Make sure we have AE/CS sign-off path for enterprise customers who might want to opt-out.

[14:35] Lucas: I'll put a draft of the metric thresholds in Miro and share.

[14:50] Maya: Okay let's do quick round-robin any last concerns?

[15:00] Amir: We should run a security checklist before any public rollout.

[15:12] Ethan: Watch for model-specific regressions; let's keep a short list of safe candidates.

[15:25] Priya: I'll own the communications plan.

[15:33] Maya: Thanks everyone. Recap: prototype throttled-mode branch, safety-net dashboards, runbook draft, shake test scheduled. Action items assigned and due dates agreed. We'll meet next week in a 30-minute sync.

[15:52] Jonah: Thanks, meeting adjourned.

End of Transcript
